chunks: From him, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A free man acknowledged that he was a slave. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He is taken according to what he said, or he pays the money.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a free man admits he is a slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *al-ijab bi al-qawl* (binding by statement) in Shia jurisprudence, where a free man’s voluntary declaration of slavery is legally enforceable. The Imam offers two resolutions: either the man remains in the status of slavery based on his testimony, or he pays the agreed-upon value (*diyya* or *thaman*) to redeem his freedom, highlighting the flexibility in resolving this specific legal anomaly.
